retained_event.headline: Renewed US-Iran fighting lifts oil above $90 while Bitcoin holds the high-$77k area
verified_event_facts: Reuters reported renewed US air strikes on Iranian targets and continued disruption risk around the Strait of Hormuz.
Reuters reported Brent settling at $94.65 and WTI at $90.22 on 2026-09-01, both up more than $4 per barrel, with supply-disruption fears tied to renewed US-Iran fighting.
Reuters reported that Iran warned it could prevent Gulf oil exports and that the Strait of Hormuz disruption remained central to energy-risk pricing.

situation_room_snapshot.authority_note: Threat and conviction are source labels only and have zero framework authority.

retained_event.market_reaction_note: Current framework data independently show BTC remaining broadly in the high-$77k region through the overnight/morning window despite the energy/geopolitical shock. This is retained as a resilience observation, not as evidence that Bitcoin is decoupled from macro risk or that the named event caused any specific price path.
retained_event.learning_note: Useful counterexample to a simple one-factor risk-off mapping: an acute oil/Hormuz shock and high yields can coexist with BTC price stability. Future value comes from comparing whether this resilience survives subsequent sessions, not from treating the event as a bullish signal.
